rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments (A.B. 325 and S.B. 763) on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: The Cartwright Act now prohibits using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade. It also prohibits using or offering a common pricing algorithm while coercing users to adopt its price or commercial-term recommendations. A pricing algorithm is common if it has two or more users and uses competitor data.
rules.key_value: Criminal fines up to the greater of $6 million or twice the gain or loss for corporations; $1 million or twice the gain or loss for individuals; civil fines up to $1 million
rules.penalty: Criminal fines of up to the greater of $6 million (businesses) or $1 million (individuals), or twice the gain or loss; civil fines up to $1 million in actions by the Attorney General or a district attorney; treble damages, injunctive relief and attorneys' fees in private suits.
rules.status_basis: Governor Newsom signed A.B. 325 and S.B. 763 in October 2025; the laws took effect on January 1, 2026.

coverage.summary: Applies to any business that uses or distributes common pricing algorithms, including apartment rental companies.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Single-firm algorithms using only a business's own data are not covered.

rules.quoted_span: The Cartwright Act now expressly prohibits (1) using or distributing common algorithms to collude on pricing, and (2) coercing users to adopt algorithmic recommendations.
